svg.title: Overwedging: a pulmonary artery trace that loses its pulse and keeps climbing
svg.desc: A pulmonary artery pressure tracing over about seven seconds. For the first two seconds it shows normal pulsatile beats with a diastolic pressure near 12 mmHg. At the point marked balloon inflated the pulsations disappear and the trace rises steadily and smoothly to nearly 40 mmHg, well above the pulmonary artery diastolic pressure, with no a or v waves. At the point marked balloon deflated the trace drops back to the pulsatile pulmonary artery pattern.

g.text: no a or v waves, pressure keeps rising
The trace should never be read. Deflate, withdraw the catheter 1 to 2 cm, and re-inflate slowly to the
smallest volume that gives a wedge.
Three signatures: a wedge at a low balloon volume, a value above the PA diastolic pressure, and a line
The flush behind the pinned tip is what drives the rise, which is also why a wedged catheter must never
